Likelihood-ratio test for nested choice models

Source: R/compare.R
lr_test.Rd

For a restricted model that is a special case of the full one: the same estimator (both mnl() or both imnl() with the same inflated alternative and link) on the same cases, with the restricted parameters a subset of the full ones (checked by name; two nested logits must share their nests, and a common inclusive value, equal_lambda = TRUE, nests the free ones); or an mnl() fit against the nlogit(), hev(), or remnl() fit with the same covariates, which tests the inclusive-value parameters against 1 (the nested-logit test of IIA), the scale parameters against 1 (homoskedastic errors), or the random-intercept standard deviations against 0.

Usage

lr_test(restricted, full)

Arguments

restricted, full

Two "choicemodel" fits on the same cases.

Value

A data frame of class "lr_test" with the statistic, degrees of freedom, and p-value; the attribute "suprema" is TRUE when a supremum replaced a separated fit's value. For the constant-share inflated multinomial logit, df is q + 1 (the share and the q further restrictions), the attribute "mixture" holds q, and p.value is NA, with a warning, when the inflated fit is degenerate (outcome coefficients diverging, or a saddle).

Details

Separation. When the data of an mnl() or rologit() fit (without unit fixed effects or inflation) are separated, the maximum-likelihood estimates do not exist and the fit stops somewhere along the separating direction; the statistic then compares the suprema of the two log-likelihoods, which separation() makes computable: 0 under complete separation, and under quasi-complete separation the value reached by moving along the separating direction and re-maximizing. Likelihood-ratio tests stay valid under separation where Wald tests do not (Rainey 2024), but with few cases or rankings per coefficient the chi-square reference can be far off; boot_lr_test() calibrates it. term_test() and combine_test() use the same suprema.

Penalized fits. Two penalized fits (firth = TRUE, or the same prior) are compared by the penalized likelihood ratio: the restricted maximum is taken over the full model's penalized log-likelihood (Heinze and Schemper 2001). The priors count as the same when they share the family, degrees of freedom, autoscaling and constants' scale, and the scales of the coefficients both fits have. A scale named for a coefficient only the full model has is ignored by the restricted fit, with a message. A penalized fit against an unpenalized one, or two different penalties, are refused.

Boundaries. Two of these restrictions sit on the boundary of the parameter space and the chi-square reference does not hold exactly. For the random-intercept model (\(\sigma = 0\)) the null distribution is a mixture of chi-squares with fewer degrees of freedom, so the reported p-value is conservative and the test can be used as such (a message says so). For the inflated model against the multinomial logit (\(\phi = 1\)) the split-equation slopes are not identified under the null, so no simple correction exists: the function refuses that pair; boot_lr_test() calibrates it by simulation (the normal reference of vuong() is not justified there either). The exception is an inflated model with one inflated alternative and an intercept-only split (y ~ x | 1, the dogit with a constant captive share): its captive odds at zero are a regular boundary point, and the reference is the 50:50 mixture of chi-square(q) and chi-square(q + 1), q the further restrictions (Self and Liang 1987), as in captivity_test(type = "lr"). The multinomial probit does not nest the multinomial logit: use vuong(). Two fits of the same family other than the multinomial logit (two HEV, nested-logit, multinomial probit, or random-intercept fits) are accepted when the restricted parameters are a subset of the full ones and the fits use the same quadrature nodes or simulation draws. The function also refuses fits with different choice sets, and a fixed-effects fit against one without fixed effects; two fixed-effects fits are compared with a message when the panels are short, since the incidental-parameters bias shifts the statistic.

Clustered data. The statistic assumes independent cases: a fit's cluster does not enter it.

References

Rainey, C. (2024). Hypothesis tests under separation. Political Analysis, 32, 172-185. doi:10.1017/pan.2023.28

Self, S.G. and Liang, K.-Y. (1987). Asymptotic properties of maximum likelihood estimators and likelihood ratio tests under nonstandard conditions. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 82, 605-610. doi:10.1080/01621459.1987.10478472

See also

boot_lr_test(), vuong(), compare_models()

Other model comparison: boot_lr_test(), classification(), compare_models(), fit_stats(), vuong()

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- rmnl(800, beta = cbind(b = c(0.5, -1, 0.8), c = c(-0.3, 0.6, -0.5)))
lr_test(mnl(y ~ x1, data = d), mnl(y ~ x1 + x2, data = d))
#> Likelihood-ratio test
#>   LR = 135.9978 on 2 df, p = < 2.2e-16
